outline.description: This chapter introduces the motivation behind the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT), contrasting it with traditional tokenization-based Large Language Models (LLMs). It explores the fundamental trade-offs between token-level and byte-level processing.
subtopics: The Role and Limitations of Tokenization (BPE)
Issues with Static Vocabularies: Domain Sensitivity and Multilingual Inequity
The Challenge of Raw Byte Modeling: Sequence Length and Computational Cost
Orthographic Knowledge and Sensitivity to Input Noise
Overview of the BLT Proposal: Dynamic Compute Allocation

outline.description: This chapter explains how BLT groups individual bytes into 'patches' to reduce the sequence length for the main transformer, focusing on the different strategies for determining patch boundaries.
subtopics: Defining the Patching Function
Static Patching: Strided Fixed-Size Groups
Heuristic Patching: Space-Based Segmentation
Entropy-Based Patching: Using a Small Byte LM for Boundary Detection
Global vs. Approximate Monotonic Constraints for Entropy
The Property of Incremental Patching and its Difference from BPE

outline.description: This chapter details the first stage of the BLT pipeline, describing how raw bytes are transformed into latent patch representations through local modeling and cross-attention.
subtopics: Role of the Local Encoder Model
Hash n-gram Embeddings: Capturing Local Context with RollPolyHash
Local Block Causal Attention Masks
Multi-Headed Cross-Attention: Pooling Bytes into Patches
Architecture of the Encoder Transformer Layers

outline.chapter_title: BLT Architecture: The Global Latent Transformer
outline.description: This chapter focuses on the central component of BLT, which processes the latent patches. It explains how the global model handles the primary computational load of the system.
subtopics: The Latent Global Transformer Model
Block-Causal Attention Masks
Processing Latent Patch Representations
Dynamic Compute Allocation: Why Patches Reduce FLOPs
Interactions Between the Local and Global Models

outline.description: This chapter describes the final stage of the BLT architecture, focusing on how the model converts global patch representations back into raw bytes.
subtopics: Role of the Local Decoder Model
Symmetry and Differences Between Encoder and Decoder
Decoder Multi-Headed Cross-Attention: Patch-to-Byte Mapping
The Decoder Transformer Layer and Byte Prediction
End-to-End Information Flow: Byte → Patch → Patch → Byte

outline.description: This chapter analyzes the scaling performance of BLT, comparing its training and inference costs with BPE-based models like Llama 3.
subtopics: Estimating FLOPs for Byte-Level Models
Compute-Optimal Scaling Trends
Training FLOP-Controlled Parity with Llama 3
Inference Efficiency: Trading Patch Size for Model Size
Fixed Inference Budget Scaling: Why Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
Bits-Per-Byte (BPB) as a Tokenizer-Independent Metric

outline.description: This chapter demonstrates the qualitative advantages of BLT over token-based models, specifically regarding noise robustness and linguistic precision.
subtopics: Evaluating Robustness to Input Noise (AntSpeak, Drop, Repeat)
Phonology and Grapheme-to-Phoneme (G2P) Tasks
The CUTE Benchmark: Testing Character-Level Manipulation
Generalization to Low-Resource Machine Translation
The Long-Tail Advantage of Raw Byte Modeling

outline.description: The final chapter discusses how to optimize BLT, including how to 'byte-ify' existing pre-trained models and an analysis of which architectural choices impact performance most.
subtopics: Distillation: Initializing BLT from Pre-trained Llama 3.1 Models
Ablation Study: The Impact of Entropy Model Size and Context Window
The Effectiveness of Hash Embeddings vs. Cross-Attention
Comparing Local Model Hyperparameters
Future Directions: End-to-End Patching and Wall-Clock Optimization
